notes.summary: @<name>:<text> now searches one entity type, also without configuration (@task:123 searched all types for task:123 before). The app can decide which entities appear in @ (mentions in tools.json) and order them by view (useMentionContext); derived labels keep every tools.json language.
notes.howTo: Check your users' habits: whenever the text before the first colon after @ is an entity type's label, alias or canonical type, the @ list now searches only that type for the rest (@task:123 searches task for 123; before, every type for task:123). Nothing to configure for that. Derived entity labels now carry every language of languages in .glirastes/tools.json, and derived action labels every language of the tool title (before only en and de); run glirastes tools refresh and review the labels. Without mentions in tools.json and without a mention context the @ list is as before, plus type suggestions while typing after @ when the chat has at least two entity types. To declare sources set mentions.policy to "declared", run glirastes tools check and paste the mention-source-candidate entries you want into mentions.sources. Call useMentionContext({ preferredTypes, presetType }) in a page below the provider to put its entity types first and preset the filter. Give entity labels and aliases per language in .glirastes/chat-interactions.json; new optional locale keys completionCommandsGroupLabel, completionEntityTypesGroupLabel, completionEntityTypeFilterLabel. An own onCompletionSelect should ignore items of type mention-filter. To show more than 8 entries per provider (12 in total), set chatInteractions.completionLimits per trigger, e.g. { "/": { "perProvider": 40, "total": 40 } }; it applies to your own completionProviders too. See docs/chat-interactions.md.

notes.summary: A derived @ entity now has the type its search tool declares by identity instead of the route's singular (media-file, not file), and its action ids follow (file.files.delete → media-file.files.delete): hidden: true patches under the old names stop applying.
notes.howTo: Run glirastes tools refresh and commit the result. For each mention-type-follows-identity finding rename, in .glirastes/chat-interactions.json, the key under entities from <old> to <new> and every action id under actions from <old>.… to <new>.… (e.g. file.files.delete → media-file.files.delete, file.open → media-file.open): a hidden: true patch under the old type or action id no longer applies, so a hidden action, also a destructive one, shows again until it is renamed; the chat-interactions handler names such patches in a console warning. Rename the old type in own code too (entity: of command arguments, defineChatEntity, chatAbout, mentionEntity, entityLinks), then add the type to mentions.acknowledgedTypes in .glirastes/tools.json. Stored messages keep {{mention:<old type>:…}} markers. A declared type that is not unique among the derived searches is not adopted (mention-type-ambiguous; the route types stay). Apps without an identity declaration on their search tools are not affected. See docs/chat-interactions.md, Migration.

notes.summary: createAiChatHandler reads a view context (what the user had open when sending the newest message) from the body field glirastesViewContext and gives it to the model as a data block. On by default; nothing sends the field yet, so an unchanged app sees no change.
notes.howTo: Nothing to do. The browser side follows in a later release. To prepare: viewContext: false turns it off (null counts as not set); viewContext: { types, maxEntries, facts: { order: z.object({ status: z.string() }) } } narrows the accepted entity types (by default every type the request's tools declare with outputEntities / inputEntities), the entries per message and the facts kept (only for a type with a schema here). history must be 'none' for now; an invalid option throws when the handler is created. The runtime container turns it off until its option chat.viewContext comes. With piiShield the values are shielded like tool results (audit: anonymize-result, counted in totalToolCalls) and checked again. The block has at most 2,966 characters (roughly 850 tokens when full); maxEntries and facts make it smaller. Only the built-in stream handler adds the block; continuations, guardrail-blocked requests, clarification answers, direct commands and a custom streamHandler get none; guardrails and hideIds do not see it. Known limit: a label is cut to 60 characters before the PII shield sees it, so a cut e-mail address, IBAN or phone number at its end may reach the model as a plain-text fragment (ids and facts are never cut); the fix follows before the browser side. Until then a client of your own that sends the field should cut labels to at most 60 characters or set viewContext: false.
